commit_message:
[HAL] Memoize allocator selects in program order (#25243)

MemoizeDeviceSelection processed its select groups in DenseMap order,
which follows attribute addresses, so the names of the generated globals
(`__allocator_select_device` vs `_device_0`, etc) changed between runs
and `.vmfb` files of multi-device modules were not reproducible. This
does not affect correctness, only the reproducibility of `.vmfb` files.

The fix uses a MapVector to process the groups in the order of their
first select.

The lit test now checks exact names instead of capturing them with `.*`
to avoid matching only the prefix part of the name.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Add LLVMCPU aarch64 and riscv64 lit tests only if LLVM has the target (#25234)

The tests
- early_data_tiling.mlir, early_data_tiling_convolution.mlir,
early_data_tiling_dynamic.mlir, added in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24969
- roundeven_native.mlir, added in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25219 (also riscv64), compile for
aarch64.

byo_llvm.sh builds LLVM with only the X86 target, so iree-compile stops
with "createTargetMachine(...) failed" and the tests fail
linux_x64_clang_byollvm job.

Add these tests in the same way as
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25221: CMake adds them only if
iree_compiler_targeting_iree_arch() is true for their architecture.

Theaarch64 and riscv64 RUN lines move into *_aarch64.mlir and
*_riscv64.mlir files, which copy the IR.

ci-extra: linux_x64_clang_byollvm

commit_message:
[CI] Let Dependabot update the Python requirements of the build tools

The PyPI deploy requirements are now a hash lock. A lock that nobody
updates turns into a set of old versions, so Dependabot regenerates it
every week. Its `uv` ecosystem runs `uv pip compile` with the options
that the lock was made with.

The entry covers all requirements files under build_tools. Two settings
keep it from changing what is set on purpose: minimum versions such as
`cmake>=3.26` stay, and `pyright` is skipped because its pin must equal
the one in the runtime's build_requirements.txt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Split constants larger than the max allocation size

A constant whose storage exceeds the max allocation size of its resource
config cannot be packed within that limit. PackConstants places such
constants in a separate resource, but the size will still exceed the limit.
The problem only shows up at runtime, when the device fails to allocate
the buffer.

This adds `iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`. It splits a private,
immutable global with an inline dense value above the limit into shards
along its outermost non-unit dimension. Each resulting shard is a contiguous
byte range of the original constant and fits into one allocation. The uses
of its loads are rewritten to use the shards:

* An input of a structured op whose split dimension is indexed by a single
  loop: the op is split along that loop with TilingInterface, one op per
  shard. The results of a parallel loop are inserted into the destination.
  The ops of a reduction loop accumulate into the previous result. This
  covers matmuls with a large weight, such as a tied LM head.
* A value read with `tensor.extract` in the body of an elementwise
  `linalg.generic`, e.g., an embedding lookup: a chain of ops, one per
  shard. Each reads its shard at the rebased, clamped index and keeps the
  previous op's element unless the index lies in its shard.

A constant with any other use is left unchanged with a warning, as is one
that cannot be split: mutable or public globals, values that are not inline
dense constants (e.g. parameters), element types not stored at 8, 16, 32 or
64 bits, or a single index of the split dimension that alone exceeds the
limit.

The limit is the max allocation size from `ResourceConfigAttr::lookup`, so
`--iree-stream-resource-max-allocation-size` unless the target sets one. It
defaults to INT64_MAX, so the pass changes nothing unless a limit is set. The
pass runs after transposes have been folded into their consumers, so that an
oversized constant is read by the op that indexes it, and before constant
expressions are hoisted and evaluated into new globals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Split constants larger than the max allocation size

A constant whose storage exceeds the max allocation size of its resource
config cannot be packed within that limit. PackConstants places such
constants in a separate resource, but the size will still exceed the limit.
The problem only shows up at runtime, when the device fails to allocate
the buffer.

This adds `iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`. It splits a private,
immutable global with an inline dense value above the limit into shards
along its outermost non-unit dimension. Each resulting shard is a contiguous
byte range of the original constant and fits into one allocation. The uses
of its loads are rewritten to use the shards:

* An input of a structured op whose split dimension is indexed by a single
  loop: the op is split along that loop with TilingInterface, one op per
  shard. The results of a parallel loop are inserted into the destination.
  The ops of a reduction loop accumulate into the previous result. This
  covers matmuls with a large weight, such as a tied LM head.
* A value read with `tensor.extract` in the body of an elementwise
  `linalg.generic`, e.g., an embedding lookup: a chain of ops, one per
  shard. Each reads its shard at the rebased, clamped index and keeps the
  previous op's element unless the index lies in its shard.

A constant with any other use is left unchanged with a warning, as is one
that cannot be split: mutable or public globals, values that are not inline
dense constants (e.g. parameters), element types not stored at 8, 16, 32 or
64 bits, or a single index of the split dimension that alone exceeds the
limit.

The limit is the max allocation size from `ResourceConfigAttr::lookup`, so
`--iree-stream-resource-max-allocation-size` unless the target sets one. It
defaults to INT64_MAX, so the pass changes nothing unless a limit is set. The
pass runs after transposes have been folded into their consumers, so that an
oversized constant is read by the op that indexes it, and before constant
expressions are hoisted and evaluated into new globals.

commit_message:
[Tracy] Bump Tracy to 0.15 (#25241)

Bumps Tracy from wolfpld/tracy@5479a42 (a post-v0.11.1 dev snapshot) to
[v0.15.0](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/releases/tag/v0.15.0)
(wolfpld/tracy@f2a4f25).
Upstream changelog:
[NEWS](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/blob/v0.15.0/NEWS). Notable
Tracy changes:
- Tracy now also Ships Prebuilt binaries for Linux and Mac (relates to
#19841)
- Loading traces from a URL in the web viewer (relates to #11957)
- Sections and a C API for them (relates to #16051)
- Messages: severity levels and filtering in the GUI
- Bugfixes, e.g. we encountered some use-after-free on Android

Changes apart from the actual bump:
- Message severities: IREE_TRACE_MESSAGE levels now map to Tracy
severities.Colors are unchanged.
- Lock events: the release is now recorded before the unlock
(iree_tracing_mutex_after_unlock → iree_tracing_mutex_before_unlock),
matching upstream. prevents anohter Thread's lock being recorded before
an unlock.
- TracyClient CMake target: IREE sets TRACY_ENABLE ON, because Tracy now
defaults it to OFF. Otherwise the exported target is empty for anything
linking it.
- No system zstd needed for iree-tracy-capture: it's built from source,
and the libzstd-devel installs in the packaging scripts are gone.
- Capture-tool dependencies: capstone moves to 6.0.0-Alpha11 and PPQSort
to 1.0.6, with upstream's patches.

Closes #21371

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bumps Tracy from wolfpld/tracy@5479a42 (a post-v0.11.1 dev snapshot) to
[v0.15.0](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/releases/tag/v0.15.0)
(wolfpld/tracy@f2a4f25).
Upstream changelog:
[NEWS](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/blob/v0.15.0/NEWS). Notable
Tracy changes:
- Tracy now also Ships Prebuilt binaries for Linux and Mac (relates to
#19841)
- Loading traces from a URL in the web viewer (relates to #11957)
- Sections and a C API for them (relates to #16051)
- Messages: severity levels and filtering in the GUI
- Bugfixes, e.g. we encountered some use-after-free on Android

Changes apart from the actual bump:
- Message severities: IREE_TRACE_MESSAGE levels now map to Tracy
severities.Colors are unchanged.
- Lock events: the release is now recorded before the unlock
(iree_tracing_mutex_after_unlock → iree_tracing_mutex_before_unlock),
matching upstream. prevents anohter Thread's lock being recorded before
an unlock.
- TracyClient CMake target: IREE sets TRACY_ENABLE ON, because Tracy now
defaults it to OFF. Otherwise the exported target is empty for anything
linking it.
- No system zstd needed for iree-tracy-capture: it's built from source,
and the libzstd-devel installs in the packaging scripts are gone.
- Capture-tool dependencies: capstone moves to 6.0.0-Alpha11 and PPQSort
to 1.0.6, with upstream's patches.

Closes #21371

commit_message:
[CI] Document the release tag ruleset

A release and its build attestations name a tag. The repository has no
tag protection, so anyone with write access can move or delete `iree-*`
and `v*` tags, and the tag is not a stable name for the commit that was
built. A ruleset that blocks updates and deletions of these tags closes
that gap.

The ruleset is a repository setting, so this records it as setup next to
the `pypi` environment and tells release managers that a release tag is
final.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[CI] Pin the PyPI deploy requirements by hash

The promote job installs change_wheel_version, pkginfo and twine to
rewrite and check the wheels, right before they are attested and
published. The requirements were unpinned, so a new or replaced release
of any of these tools or of their dependencies would run in the next
publish and could alter the wheels unnoticed.

Pin all of them by hash. pypi_deploy_requirements.in keeps the list of
tools, and pypi_deploy_requirements.txt is compiled from it with
`uv pip compile --universal`, so that the same file installs on every
platform and Python version that pypi_deploy.sh runs on. The workflow
also refuses source distributions, because building one would pull in
further packages that are not pinned.

pypi_deploy.sh now reads the tool names from the .in file, because its
check cannot parse the compiled file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

The promote job installs change_wheel_version, pkginfo and twine to
rewrite and check the wheels, right before they are attested and
published. The requirements were unpinned, so a new or replaced release
of any of these tools or of their dependencies would run in the next
publish and could alter the wheels unnoticed.

Pin all of them by hash. pypi_deploy_requirements.in keeps the list of
tools, and pypi_deploy_requirements.txt is compiled from it with
`uv pip compile --universal`, so that the same file installs on every
platform and Python version that pypi_deploy.sh runs on. The workflow
also refuses source distributions, because building one would pull in
further packages that are not pinned.

pypi_deploy.sh now reads the tool names from the .in file, because its
check cannot parse the compiled file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Default the export source location line to 0 (#25239)

LLVMCPUTarget fills an export's SourceLocation only when the debug level
is at least 1 and the export's location contains a file location.
Otherwise `line` stayed uninitialized and LibraryBuilder write random
bytes from the stack into the source location table of the executable
library.

The issue makes .vmfb files non-reproducible: compiling the same input
twice gives different bytes/checksums. It doesn't happen to all inputs,
only to some, e.g. TOSA bytecode from the TFLite converter, where every
op has `loc(unknown)`.

Default `line` to 0, like the other integer fields of structs in the
same module.

Tested by compiling four TFLite models multiple times with the llvm-cpu
backend and comparing binaries: before the change every new recompile
was different from the first one, after the fix all were identical.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Default the export source location line to 0 (#25239)

LLVMCPUTarget fills an export's SourceLocation only when the debug level
is at least 1 and the export's location contains a file location.
Otherwise `line` stayed uninitialized and LibraryBuilder write random
bytes from the stack into the source location table of the executable
library.

The issue makes .vmfb files non-reproducible: compiling the same input
twice gives different bytes/checksums. It doesn't happen to all inputs,
only to some, e.g. TOSA bytecode from the TFLite converter, where every
op has `loc(unknown)`.

Default `line` to 0, like the other integer fields of structs in the
same module.

Tested by compiling four TFLite models multiple times with the llvm-cpu
backend and comparing binaries: before the change every new recompile
was different from the first one, after the fix all were identical.

commit_message:
[HAL] Memoize allocator selects in program order (#25243)

MemoizeDeviceSelection processed its select groups in DenseMap order,
which follows attribute addresses, so the names of the generated globals
(`__allocator_select_device` vs `_device_0`, etc) changed between runs
and `.vmfb` files of multi-device modules were not reproducible. This
does not affect correctness, only the reproducibility of `.vmfb` files.

The fix uses a MapVector to process the groups in the order of their
first select.

The lit test now checks exact names instead of capturing them with `.*`
to avoid matching only the prefix part of the name.

commit_message:
[CI] Skip the POSIX async socket tests in linux_x64_clang_byollvm

iree/async/platform/posix/cts/socket_tests times out in every
linux_x64_clang_byollvm run since the ubuntu-24.04 runner image moved
to kernel 7.0.0-1017-azure. The test log stops at
CTS/SocketPosixTest.UnixDgram_ConnectedLoopback/posix_poll.

That kernel has a NULL pointer dereference in AppArmor, fixed upstream
by https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/4de32fd05ce9. It triggers
when an AppArmor-confined process uses write() or writev() on a
connected AF_UNIX datagram socket. This test is the first one that does
so. The fault ends only the calling thread. The worker threads of the
proactor stay alive, so the process prints nothing more and waits until
ctest stops it.

Only this job is affected because it is the only one that runs the
tests in a container on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 image. Docker
confines the container with its default AppArmor profile. The runtime
jobs use the same image without a container, so their processes are not
confined and the test passes there.

The kernel log of the runner was not available. The cause follows from
the kernel source of that build and from the upstream fix, which
reports the same call path.

The test still runs in the other Linux jobs. Remove the exclusion when
the runner image has a kernel with the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[CI] Skip the POSIX async socket tests in linux_x64_clang_byollvm

iree/async/platform/posix/cts/socket_tests times out in every
linux_x64_clang_byollvm run since the ubuntu-24.04 runner image moved
to kernel 7.0.0-1017-azure. The test log stops at
CTS/SocketPosixTest.UnixDgram_ConnectedLoopback/posix_poll.

That kernel has a NULL pointer dereference in AppArmor, fixed upstream
by https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/4de32fd05ce9. It triggers
when an AppArmor-confined process uses write() or writev() on a
connected AF_UNIX datagram socket. This test is the first one that does
so. The fault ends only the calling thread. The worker threads of the
proactor stay alive, so the process prints nothing more and waits until
ctest stops it.

Only this job is affected because it is the only one that runs the
tests in a container on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 image. Docker
confines the container with its default AppArmor profile. The runtime
jobs use the same image without a container, so their processes are not
confined and the test passes there.

The kernel log of the runner was not available. The cause follows from
the kernel source of that build and from the upstream fix, which
reports the same call path.

The test still runs in the other Linux jobs. Remove the exclusion when
the runner image has a kernel with the fix.

by https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/4de32fd05ce9. It triggers
when an AppArmor-confined process uses write() or writev() on a
connected AF_UNIX datagram socket. This test is the first one that does
so. The fault ends only the calling thread. The worker threads of the
proactor stay alive, so the process prints nothing more and waits until
ctest stops it.

Only this job is affected because it is the only one that runs the
tests in a container on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 image. Docker
confines the container with its default AppArmor profile. The runtime
jobs use the same image without a container, so their processes are not
confined and the test passes there.

The kernel log of the runner was not available. The cause follows from
the kernel source of that build and from the upstream fix, which
reports the same call path.

The test still runs in the other Linux jobs. Remove the exclusion when
the runner image has a kernel with the fix.

commit_message:
[HAL] Memoize allocator selects in program order (#25243)

MemoizeDeviceSelection processed its select groups in DenseMap order,
which follows attribute addresses, so the names of the generated globals
(`__allocator_select_device` vs `_device_0`, etc) changed between runs
and `.vmfb` files of multi-device modules were not reproducible. This
does not affect correctness, only the reproducibility of `.vmfb` files.

The fix uses a MapVector to process the groups in the order of their
first select.

The lit test now checks exact names instead of capturing them with `.*`
to avoid matching only the prefix part of the name.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
